Estimate group classes with fixed individual profile definitions

Source: R/fixed-measurement.R
fit_staged.Rd

fit_staged() estimates a multilevel mixture model in which observed groups are distinguished by their composition of individual profiles. It separates the estimation of profile definitions from the estimation of group classes, allowing between-group differences to be studied while retaining a common measurement model.

The first stage estimates the individual profiles using a model with one group class. These profiles are defined by their indicator distributions, including means and covariance parameters for continuous indicators and response probabilities for categorical indicators. The second stage holds these measurement parameters fixed and estimates the profile probabilities within each group class, together with the proportions of the group classes. Group classes therefore differ in their profile composition while the profiles retain the same measurement definitions.

A compatible fitted measurement model may also be supplied, allowing established profile definitions to be reused. The returned model contains the second-stage estimates and retains the first-stage fit, so both stages can be inspected.

Usage

fit_staged(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  n_group_classes = 2L,
  measurement = NULL,
  variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  min_variance = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "fiml"),
  covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
  categorical = character(),
  min_probability = 1e-10,
  time = NULL,
  search = NULL,
  n_screen = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the indicators and the group identifier.

vars

Unique character vector of indicator column names. Indicators named in categorical use categorical response distributions; the remaining indicators are continuous and use Gaussian distributions.

id

Name of the observed group identifier column. Character, factor and numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not. Required; id = NULL is not accepted.

n_profiles

Positive integer number of individual profiles.

n_group_classes

Number of latent group classes in the second stage. Must be at least two; the default is 2.

measurement

An optional fitted multilpa model supplying the first-stage measurement estimates. With NULL (the default), the first stage is estimated from data. A supplied model must have one group class and matching profiles, indicators and measurement options. Models with weights, centering, scaling, ordinal or count indicators, direct_effects, or local_dependence between continuous indicators are not supported. Supported covariance structures are EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV. An incompatible measurement model raises latents_bad_stage.

variance_model

"varying" (the default; profile-specific variances or covariance matrices) or "equal" (shared across profiles).

n_starts

Number of EM starts used in each estimated stage. When measurement is supplied, only the second stage is estimated.

max_iter

Nonnegative integer maximum number of EM updates per start in each estimated stage (default 1000). Zero evaluates initial values without performing EM updates.

tol

Positive convergence tolerance (default 1e-8). EM has converged when one step (or SQUAREM cycle) changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of observed indicator values (each non-missing cell in a row of positive weight, with a minimum count of one). The tolerance is therefore expressed per observed indicator value.

min_variance

Lower bound on each continuous-indicator variance, or on each covariance eigenvalue under full covariance. NULL (the default) uses 1e-6 times the smallest observed sample variance of the continuous indicators. A numeric value specifies an absolute bound in squared indicator units. Estimates at the bound raise a warning. In the second stage, measurement parameters are held at their first-stage values.

seed

Optional random seed: any integer set.seed() accepts, including negative integers. When supplied, the caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

"error" (the default) rejects missing indicators; "fiml" maximises the observed-data likelihood under an ignorable missingness mechanism (MAR), integrating over missing indicators.

covariance_model

"diagonal" (the default) assumes conditional independence; "full" estimates within-profile residual covariances.

categorical

Character vector naming indicators to treat as categorical. Each is modelled by unrestricted, profile-specific response probabilities over its observed categories (the latent class measurement model); binary, ordinal and unordered indicators are handled by the same parameterization. Numeric, integer, logical, character and factor columns are accepted. Indicators not named here stay Gaussian, so naming a subset fits a mixed-mode model.

min_probability

Positive lower bound on every categorical response probability (default 1e-10), constraining the maximum-likelihood problem as min_variance does for Gaussian indicators.

time

Optional name of a column giving each observation's position within its group, such as a wave, occasion or course number. It is not used in estimation; it is stored for get_results(x, "sequences"), get_results(x, "sequence_summary") and plot(what = "sequences"). Values must be complete and unique within each group, and are ordered as sort() orders them: numbers numerically, a factor by its levels, and character strings alphabetically. Numbers stored as text whose alphabetical order is not their numeric order ("2", "10"), and numbered labels sharing their text around the number whose alphabetical order is not the numbers' ("T2", "T10"; "week 2", "week 10"), raise latents_bad_time (also latents_bad_data); give the order with factor(levels = ) or zero-pad the numbers. Zero-padded numbers and ISO dates are accepted.

search

Initialisation strategy for each estimated stage: NULL (the default), "kmeans" or "emEM". The default is "emEM" for models containing continuous indicators with a shared covariance matrix (EEI or EEE), and "kmeans" otherwise. "kmeans" uses clustering-based starts; "emEM" screens a pool of starts with short EM runs before completing n_starts selected searches. The second stage uses the first-stage measurement estimates as supplied starting values and holds them fixed. See multilpa() for the screening and start-selection procedure.

n_screen

Number of starts screened under search = "emEM", at least n_starts. The default is five times n_starts. Screening is skipped in the second stage when n_starts = 1, because a starting measurement solution is supplied. A value with search = "kmeans", or one below n_starts, raises latents_bad_argument.

Value

A second-stage multilpa object with measurement parameters equal to the first-stage estimates. The fixed component identifies the parameter blocks held constant. n_parameters counts the parameters estimated in the second stage; n_parameters_with_measurement also includes the first-stage measurement parameters. get_results(fit, what = "stages") returns a two-row summary of the estimation stages. Standard result-extraction and diagnostic methods for multilpa objects are available.

Details

Information criteria and likelihood-ratio comparisons condition on the fixed measurement model.

With parameter_inference(fit, method = "bootstrap"), groups are resampled and both stages are re-estimated. This procedure propagates first-stage estimation uncertainty and reports standard errors and intervals for the measurement parameters as well as the second-stage parameters. A supplied measurement model is re-estimated in each resample using its fitting options.

For staged models with the same fixed measurement specification, use n_parameters when comparing conditional information criteria. Comparisons with jointly estimated models can include the measurement parameters through n_parameters_with_measurement, but remain descriptive because the staged estimates do not generally maximize the joint likelihood.

Interpretation

The second-stage estimates are conditional on the fixed measurement model. Default Wald standard errors omit uncertainty from estimating that model; bootstrap inference can propagate this uncertainty by resampling groups and re-estimating both stages. Staged estimates do not generally maximise the joint likelihood, so comparisons with jointly estimated models require care.

See also

multilpa() for selective constraints through fixed; starting_values() with what = "measurement" to extract measurement parameters for a subsequent fit.

Examples

set.seed(7)
example_data <- data.frame(
  school = rep(seq_len(30), each = 8),
  score_a = stats::rnorm(240), score_b = stats::rnorm(240)
)
staged <- fit_staged(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                     n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 2,
                     seed = 1)
get_results(staged, what = "stages")
#>         stage group_classes            fixed log_likelihood parameters
#> 1 measurement             1             <NA>      -671.8928          9
#> 2  membership             2 means, variances      -671.8928          3
#>   parameters_with_measurement converged
#> 1                           9      TRUE
#> 2                          11      TRUE
get_results(staged, what = "profile_probabilities")
#>   group_class profile probability group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1   0.9782787                     0.5
#> 2           1       2   0.0217213                     0.5
#> 3           2       1   0.9782787                     0.5
#> 4           2       2   0.0217213                     0.5
